references.text: The preceding context: The parable is told because Jesus was near Jerusalem and people thought the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately ([ref:Luk 19:11|Luke 19:11]). The man's journey to a distant country to receive kingly power corrects the expectation of an immediate kingdom.

Jesus compares himself to a man who goes abroad and entrusts responsibility to his servants – a similar motif concerning the master's absence and the servants' stewardship ([ref:Mark 13:34|Mark 13:34]).
The parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:14-15|Matthew 25:14-15] has a closely parallel motif: a man who goes to a foreign country and entrusts his servants with values they are to manage.
In the parable of the vineyard workers ([ref:Matt 21:33-39|Matthew 21:33-39]), the owner goes abroad and expects fruit from his servants – a motif resembling the nobleman's departure in Luke 19:12.

Daniel's vision of "one like a son of man" who comes before the Ancient of Days and receives dominion, glory, and a kingdom ([ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]). This can be seen as the Old Testament background for the image of one who goes away to receive kingly authority.

In the parable of the vineyard tenants, Jesus mentions a man who planted a vineyard and went abroad for a long time ([ref:Luk 20:9|Luke 20:9]) – a similar motif involving a master's prolonged absence.

After the resurrection, the disciples ask if Jesus will now restore the kingdom to Israel. Jesus answers that times and seasons are not for them to know ([ref:Apg 1:6-7|Acts 1:6-7]). This reflects the same theme as the parable: the kingdom does not come immediately, but after a period of absence.

Jesus' ascension and the promise of his return ([ref:Apg 1:9-11|Acts 1:9-11]) can be seen as the fulfillment of the image in the parable – the nobleman's departure to receive kingly power and then return.

Paul writes that God has exalted Christ and given him the name above every name ([ref:Fil 2:9-11|Philippians 2:9-11]). This reflects that Jesus, after his "departure" from earth, has received kingly power and dominion.

The kingdom of the world has become our Lord's and his Anointed One's ([ref:Åp 11:15|Revelation 11:15]). Here the image of the nobleman who goes away to receive kingly power and returns as king is fulfilled.
